transcript.text: I need to flag a serious issue with the online ballot component of the draft plan. I tested the platform this morning and found that it records each voter's identity for 90 days, and that recording function cannot be disabled. This means any student who votes would have their identity tied to their ballot stored electronically for three months. Given student privacy and safety concerns — especially in light of what Ms. Ellis has raised — I don't think we can proceed with the online ballot as currently drafted. The approved workaround is sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, with zero electronic voter records. I have not yet updated the election plan to reflect this, but the draft plan's reliance on an online ballot needs to be replaced before Dr. Morgan approves it.

transcript.text: I need to share the substance of my confidential student-safety review. My review found a substantiated retaliation concern involving two students who are part of this election. Because of this, our student-privacy protocol requires anonymous voting and prohibits releasing vote totals until the election is certified. I've kept the full review in my counseling file since it contains protected student information, and I have not yet briefed Dr. Morgan on the specifics. What this means for the draft plan is that the current provision to publish vote totals at the end of election day must be removed or delayed until certification, and we must ensure voting is fully anonymous. Mr. Shah's paper ballot workaround aligns with this requirement, but the vote totals publication issue still needs to be addressed before Dr. Morgan approves the plan.
